lesson.scenario: A partition router adds node N3 to a versioned hash ring and migrates only the newly owned clockwise range.

steps.title: Publish the initial ring
steps.narration: Epoch 11 contains N1@10, N2@40, and N4@90; ranges wrap clockwise.
steps.outcome: Each hash position has exactly one primary clockwise successor.
steps.invariant: All routers use an immutable ring epoch for a request.

steps.title: Route existing keys
steps.narration: alpha@35 resolves to N2 and beta@65 resolves to N4 under epoch 11.
steps.outcome: Routing requires one hash and a clockwise token lookup.
steps.invariant: The owner is the first token greater than or equal to the key hash, with wraparound.

steps.title: Insert joining token
steps.narration: The controller prepares epoch 12 with N3@70 between N2 and N4.
steps.outcome: Only N4's former subrange (40,70] changes ownership in the staged ring.
steps.invariant: The active epoch does not change before required range data is copied.

steps.title: Stream the affected range
steps.narration: The mover copies beta@65 and its version while writes in (40,70] are dual-recorded to N4 and N3.
action: copy beta and catch up range log
steps.outcome: N3 has a complete copy through the cutover log position.
steps.invariant: Migration copies only keys whose hashes fall in the joining node's predecessor range.

steps.title: Atomically publish epoch 12
steps.narration: Routers switch to epoch 12, making N3 primary for beta while alpha remains on N2.
steps.outcome: Only beta changes primary owner, and replica successors are recomputed.
steps.invariant: A request routes entirely with either epoch 11 or epoch 12, never a mixed view.

steps.title: Retire the old primary copy
steps.narration: After epoch-11 requests drain, N4 retains beta only as N3's clockwise replica and range migration completes.
steps.outcome: The ring is balanced without moving alpha or unrelated ranges.
steps.invariant: Old ownership is removed only after new ownership is durable and old-epoch traffic has drained.

production.scenario: A CDN edge layer places cache keys on a changing fleet of regional caches.
components: cache clients that route asset lookups
flows: The edge path needs the right cache owner before serving a static asset.
read ring epoch and namespace metadata
The router resolves the current cache membership and asset namespace.
The key and ring epoch are handed to the placement engine as one routing decision.
assign key to clockwise ring owners
The mechanism selects the cache node set responsible for this key.
record hit or miss by owner
Serving nodes publish placement outcomes for later rebalancing and audits.
signal hot partition or draining node
The boundary surfaces unhealthy ownership concentration before it causes an outage.
add virtual capacity or reroute around failure
Operations adjust placement inputs without changing caller behavior.
